error.statement: A numerical SVG approximation to the analytic sine, not a claim that a cubic equals sine identically. Exact knot incidence and endpoint slopes are preserved to the stated serialization tolerance.

checks.proof: Each serialized cubic has affine x and Hermite endpoint data sin(x), cos(x). For sine, |f^(4)|<=1, so the Hermite remainder is bounded by h^4/384 on every interval. Canonical origin and +/-pi/2 data are exactly 0,+/-1 and slopes 1,0 before decimal serialization.

Every piece has derivative Bernstein controls of the sign of cos on its interval. Knots include both extrema. Thus there is exactly one trough and one crest, with no additional turns. All y-control values lie in [-1,1]; x is strictly increasing. Both crop endpoints stay within (-pi,pi), with opposite signs of sine.

All positive-x cubic control values satisfy y<=x, and all negative-x controls satisfy y>=x. The line difference is a Bernstein cubic, so no false diagonal crossing is introduced. All control values have y<=1, so the horizontal tangent is not crossed. Equality at the origin/crest is accompanied by the verified derivative slope.

Equal screen scales preserve the y=x bisector; the two exact tangent segments meet at (1,1), left of pi/2. Native incidence/connects/perpendicular/parallel/displacement assertions separately bind the actual spec endpoints.

limitation: FigureSpec has no native analytic sine/tangency assertion type. This author evidence verifies the actual serialized path; it supplements, not replaces, the separate source-first independent mathematical/visual review.
